own_solution.law: For non-relativistic motion, K = p²/(2m) and λ = h/p = hc/√(2mc²K). With K = 150 eV and mc² = 511000 eV, λ = 1240/√(153300000) nm.
assumptions: The electron is treated non-relativistically as specified.
The separate apparatus does not interact with the electron.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TB701 and T42DA omit the numerical value and unit supplied as 90 eV in the other variants, so the sentences do not satisfy the required same-number-and-unit condition.

notes: The base physics is well-posed. T3024 and T6CB4 increase the electron's final kinetic energy to 240 eV, giving λ = 1240/√(2 × 511000 × 240) nm. All proton and alpha-particle additions are disconnected from the target. Their unspecified energy increments do not prevent determining the electron wavelength; the invalid verdict concerns the required variant matching.
